# Page 22^page=22
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 22 Daily Content PDF NATIONAL AFFAIRS PM Narendra Modi Virtually Launches ‘Karmayogi Sadhana Saptah 2026’ for Civil Servants On April 2, 2026, Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi virtually launched the ‘Karmayogi Sadhana Saptah 2026’, a national learning week initiative under Mission Karmayogi celebrating its five-year milestone, at the Dr. Ambedkar International Centre (DAIC), New Delhi (Delhi). • He emphasized that governance must adapt to changing needs with ‘Nagrik Devo Bhava,’ urging continuous learning, tech-and data-driven decision-making, and duty-oriented public service to achieve Viksit Bharat 2047. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Launch of Karmayogi Sadhana Saptah 2026 ✓ By Whom? PM Narendra Modi ✓ Significance: Marking 5 years of Mission Karmayogi. ✓ Organizer: Capacity Building Commission (CBC) ✓ Timeline: April 2 to 8, 2026 ✓ Objective: Strengthen civil servants’ capabilities, commitment, citizen-centric orientation ✓ Key Platform: iGOT Karmayogi ✓ Key Initiatives: Karmayogi Geet, Kshamata Connect, Kartavya Karyakram, Peer Assessment Framework ✓ New Tech: AI-powered Case Study Suite for Amrit Gyaan Kosh (AGK). ✓ Alignment: Viksit Bharat 2047. About Karmayogi Sadhana Saptah: Organiser: Sadhana (Strengthening Adaptive Development and Humane Aptitude for National Advancement) Saptah, one of India’s largest collaborative civil services capacity-building efforts, is organised by the Capacity Building Commission (CBC), the executive body of the Mission Karmayogi, from April 2 to 8, 2026. Participants: The initiative unites Ministries, States, and Civil Services Training Institutions under a shared nationwide learning framework. Pillars: The programme is built on three pillars: Technology, Tradition, and Tangible Outcomes, and includes workshops, masterclasses, and institutional deliberations to strengthen a future-ready governance ecosystem. Launch of Key Initiatives: During the inaugural session, several key initiatives were launched to enhance large-scale capacity building. Karmayogi Geet: Produced by the CBC, the song inspires selfless service, integrity, and commitment among civil servants, reinforcing the ethos of nation-building. Kshamata Connect: Delivered through the Integrated Government Online Training (iGOT) Karmayogi platform in multiple regional languages, this initiative equips frontline officials with knowledge on national priorities, participatory governance, digital safety, and emerging technologies. Kartavya Karyakram: A nationwide behavioural training programme covering around 1.3 crore officials, it promotes Seva Bhav through digital learning, in-person sessions, and group discussions to improve responsiveness and accountability. Peer Assessment Framework: The trust-based assessment system on iGOT Karmayogi evaluates skills through peer and supervisory reviews, linking learning with practical application and fostering outcome-

# Page 23^page=23
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 23 Daily Content PDF driven capacity building. AI Case Suite: The Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered Case Study Suite for Amrit Gyaan Kosh (AGK), developed with Civic Innovation Foundation (Civis), includes tools like Case Study Analyzer and CaseConnect to support case-based learning and curriculum integration. About Mission Karmayogi: Background: The National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building (NPCSCB) – Mission Karmayogi, approved by the Government of India (GoI) on 2nd September 2020, aims to build a competent civil service rooted in Indian ethos. Digital Platform: The iGOT Karmayogi platform, launched in 2022, serves as the digital backbone of the mission, providing a comprehensive learning ecosystem for civil servants across India. Key Pillars: The mission is structured around four pillars: Policy Framework, Institutional Framework, Competency Framework, and Digital Learning Framework (iGOT-Karmayogi), supported by the electronic Human Resource Management System (e-HRMS) and the Monitoring and Evaluation Framework. About Capacity Building Commission(CBC): Establishment: The CBC was established on April 1, 2021, as part of the National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building (NPCSCB) – Mission Karmayogi. Role: The commission designs frameworks, sets standards, and fosters collaboration to make governance transparent, accountable, citizen-centric, and future-ready. Custodian: CBC serves as the custodian of the Mission Karmayogi framework, driving civil service reforms through capacity-building and competency-based learning. Chairperson- S. Radha Chauhan Headquarters- New Delhi, Delhi CBDT Launches ‘Kar Saathi’ Website to Simplify Tax Filing In April 2026, the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), under the Department of Revenue (DoR), Ministry of Finance (MoF), launched a new website and an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered assistant called ‘Kar Saathi’ to simplify the procedure of tax filing. • The launch of the web portal coincides with a nationwide awareness campaign, Policy Reform and Responsible Action for Mission Viksit Bharat (PRARAMBH 2026). Exam Hints: ✓ What? Launch of Website ‘Kar Saathi’ ✓ Launched by: CBDT ✓ Purpose: To simplify the process of tax filing ✓ Compliance with: IT Act, 2025 ✓ Feature: 24×7 AI support (Hindi & English) ✓ Campaign: PRARAMBH 2026. About ‘Kar Saathi’ Portal: Tax Filing: The newly launched ‘Kar Saathi’ portal offers round-the-clock support to assist taxpayers with queries and compliance under the Income Tax Act, 2025. • It includes an AI chatbot that provides instant tax- related information in both Hindi and English. Unified Platform: The new website consolidates all the information related to income tax, including forms, filing procedures, and guidelines, in a unified platform. Key Progress: Since the inception of PRARAMBH programme in March 2026, rules have been reduced from 510 to 333 and forms from 399 to 190, thereby eliminating requirements for more than six crore transactions.

# Page 24^page=24
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 24 Daily Content PDF UIDAI and MapmyIndia Partner to Enable Authorised Aadhaar Centres on Mappls App In April 2026, the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), signed an agreement with MapmyIndia to integrate authorised Aadhaar service centres into the Mappls Application(app). Exam Hints: ✓ What? Agreement signed ✓ Entities: UIDAI & MapmyIndia ✓ Purpose: To integrate authorised Aadhaar centres on Mappls App ✓ Services: Adult & child enrolment, address & mobile updates ✓ Coverage: ASKs and authorised centres across India. Key Details: Objective: The initiative aims to improve public convenience, ensure seamless access to Aadhaar services, and reduce misinformation regarding unauthorised centres. Features: The app allows users to filter searches by specific Aadhaar services and navigate to authorised centres with accurate results. • It enables identification of centres offering services such as adult enrolment, child enrolment, and updates to address or mobile number. Coverage: The initiative will include Aadhaar Seva Kendras (ASKs) along with other authorised Aadhaar centres, ensuring distinct and accurate listings. Microsoft Establish AI Skill Center in Chandigarh University to Enhance Employability In April 2026, Microsoft signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Chandigarh University (CU), Punjab, to set up a state-of-the-art Artificial Intelligence (AI) Skill Center at its Mohali campus, aimed at enhancing digital skills and employability. • The centre was inaugurated by Sanjay Dhingra, Director of Public Sector at Microsoft, alongside officials from byteXL and senior leadership from Chandigarh University. Exam Hints: ✓ What? MoU signed to establish AI Skill Center ✓ Entities: Microsoft & Chandigarh University ✓ Where? Chandigarh University, Punjab ✓ Focus Areas: AI, ML, Cloud Computing, Data Science, Cybersecurity ✓ Key Courses: AZ-900, DP-900, AI-900 ✓ Platform: Microsoft Azure (Virtual Labs) ✓ Partner: byteXL. About Microsoft AI Skill Center: Certifications: The center will offer globally recognized Microsoft certifications in AI, Machine Learning (ML), Cloud Computing (CC), Data Science, and Cybersecurity, including AZ-900 (Azure Fundamentals), DP- 900 (Data Fundamentals), and AI-900 (AI Fundamentals). Training: Students will have access to over 4,400 Microsoft learning modules linked to job roles, with hands-on lab-based training, virtual labs on Microsoft Azure, and real-world project experience. Collaboration: CU will launch a specialized Bachelor of Engineering (BE) in Computer Science Engineering (CSE) with AI specialization, online Master of Computer Applications (MCA) courses, and partner with byteXL for AI, ML, and Generative AI (GenAI)-focused programs. Initiative: Microsoft’s courses and certifications will be made accessible to all students, supporting the ‘AI for All’ initiative.

# Page 25^page=25
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 25 Daily Content PDF Israel’s PLR Systems Delivers First Batch of NEGEV LMGs to India On 1 April 2026, Israel Weapon Industries (IWI) announced the delivery of the first batch of 2,000 NEGEV 7.62×51 Light Machine Guns (LMGs) to India. The delivery was carried out by PLR Systems, a joint venture (JV) between IWI and the Adani Group, marking a significant milestone under the ‘Make in India’ initiative with technology transfer. • The delivery is part of a larger August 2024 contract for 41,000 LMGs, with another 4,000 units to be supplied by end-2026. Exam Hints: ✓ What? First Batch of NEGEV 7.62×51 LMGs delivered ✓ Announced by: Israel Weapon Industries (IWI) ✓ Delivered by: PLR Systems ✓ Quantity: 2,000 delivered ✓ Initiative: Make in India, Technology Transfer ✓ Manufacturing: Malanpur, MP ✓ Feature: 7.62 mm, semi & automatic modes About NEGEV Light Machine Guns: Manufacturer: PLR Systems, India’s first private-sector company to manufacture small arms and ammunition, is producing the NEGEV LMGs at its facility in Malanpur, Madhya Pradesh (MP). Weapon: The NEGEV 7.62×51 LMG, used by the Israel Defence Forces (IDF), fires 7.62 millimetre (mm) ammunition, supports semi- and fully automatic modes, and is effective against fortified targets in high- intensity and urban combat. Features: It is lightweight, highly reliable in harsh conditions, equipped with Picatinny rails and tritium night sights, North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO)-compliant, and adaptable for use on helicopters, vehicles, and naval platforms. Partnership: PLR Systems has also secured a contract to supply 170,000 Close-Quarter Battle (CQB) carbines, with the first batch of 18,000 units expected to be delivered in 2026 BANKING & FINANCE IRDAI Designates LIC, GIC Re, and NIACL as D-SIIs for FY26 In April 2026, the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) designated Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), The New India Assurance Company Limited (NIACL) and General Insurance Corporation of India (GIC Re) as Domestic-Systemically Important Insurers (D-SIIs) for Financial Year 2025-26 (FY26). • IRDAI has clarified that the list of D-SIIs remains unchanged from the previous financial year. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Designation of 3 Insurers as D-SIIs for FY26 ✓ Name Insurers: LIC, NIACL and GIC Re ✓ Designated by: IRDAI About D-SIIs: Definition: It refers to insurers of large size, market importance and domestic and global inter- connectedness whose distress or failure would cause a significant impact on the domestic financial system. Therefore, the continued functioning of these insurers is important for the uninterrupted availability of insurance services to the national economy. • D-SIIs are insurance companies identified by IRDAI, perceived as insurers that are ‘too big or too important to fail’ (TBTF).

# Page 26^page=26
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 26 Daily Content PDF Background: In January 2019, IRDAI formed a committee on D-SIIs in the backdrop of the International Association of Insurance Supervisors (IAIS), a voluntary membership organization of insurance supervisors from over 200 jurisdictions, directing all member countries to have a regulatory framework to deal with D- SIIs. • The 1st list of D-SIIs was introduced in September 2020 and since then, only the same three state- owned insurers have been identified annually: LIC; GIC Re and NIACL. Key Parameters: IRDAI outlined key parameters for the identification and supervision of D-SIIs which include: size of operations in terms of total revenue (including premium underwritten and the value of assets under management) and global activities across more than one jurisdiction. About Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI): IRDAI was established under the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999. It is an autonomous body under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Finance (MoF) responsible for regulating and developing the insurance and re-insurance industries in India. Chairperson – Ajay Seth Headquarters – Hyderabad, Telangana Established – 1999 ECONOMY & BUSINESS NSE and IGX Partner to Launch India’s First Domestic Benchmark Natural Gas Derivatives On April 1 2026, the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE), India’s leading stock exchange, announced a strategic collaboration with Indian Gas Exchange Limited (IGX), India’s first automated national-level gas trading platform, to launch India’s first exchange-traded natural gas derivatives based on a domestic benchmark, aimed at improving risk management in the gas market. • The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has approved the initiative, with the launch date to be announced soon. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Launch of India’s first domestic benchmarked natural gas derivatives ✓ By Whom? NSE and IGX ✓ Purpose: Risk management and domestic price discovery ✓ Index: GIXI (Gas IndeX of India) ✓ Regulator: SEBI. About Natural Gas Derivatives Initiative: Product: The NSE will introduce Indian Natural Gas Futures contracts based on the Gas IndeX of India (GIXI) developed by IGX, with pricing linked to actual trades on the IGX platform. Benefits: The initiative will provide efficient risk management tools for producers, consumers, financial institutions, brokers, and investors, while enhancing market efficiency, liquidity, and transparency in India’s gas market. IGX: Operating under the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB), it facilitates natural gas trading and price discovery, supporting NSE’s expansion into domestically benchmarked commodity derivatives.

# Page 27^page=27
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 27 Daily Content PDF AWARDS & RECOGNITIONS Uttarakhand & Odisha Police Honoured with President’s Police Colours In April 2026, the President of India Droupadi Murmu approved the conferment of the President’s Police Colour (Nishaan), the highest national honour for a state police force, on the Uttarakhand Police and Odisha Police in recognition of their exceptional service, professionalism, and commitment to internal security and public safety. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Conferment of President’s Police Colours (Nishaan) ✓ To Whom? Uttarakhand & Odisha Police ✓ Approved by: President of India Droupadi Murmu ✓ Purpose: Recognition of service, bravery, professionalism & long-term contribution. About Uttarakhand Police: Award: The Uttarakhand Police was honoured for its bravery, discipline, professional excellence, and long- term dedication to the nation during the state’s Silver Jubilee year. • Uttarakhand has become the 16th state in the country to receive the President’s Police Colour for distinguished policing. Leadership: Uttarakhand’s Chief Minister (CM) Pushkar Singh Dhami and Director General of Police (DGP) Deepam Seth guided the force, which is acknowledged for its service in disaster management, notably the 2013 Kedarnath tragedy, and managing large-scale events like the Maha Kumbh and Char Dham Yatra. About Odisha Police: Award: The Odisha Police was conferred the award for recognising exceptional discipline, service excellence, bravery, professionalism, and long-term institutional contribution, coinciding with the 90th Police Foundation Day (Utkal Divas). Leadership: Odisha’s Director General of Police (DGP) Y B Khurania and Additional Director General (ADG) Prateek Mohanty led the force, which has been operational since 1936 and is acknowledged for anti-Maoist operations, crime prevention, and citizen-centric initiatives. About President’s Police Colour: Award: The President’s Police Colours is the highest institutional recognition for police organisations in India, awarded for discipline, bravery, professional excellence, law and order maintenance, public safety contributions, and long-term service. Origin: The President’s Police Colour, established on 27th May 1951, evolved from the colonial “King’s Colours” military tradition and was adapted as the “President’s Colours” after India became a republic in 1950. Eligibility: Conferred on police units with a minimum of 25 years of distinguished service, following a rigorous multi-layered evaluation by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) of crime control, bravery, discipline, and institutional milestones. Representation: The award is symbolised by a ceremonial flag and a unique insignia worn on the left sleeve of the police uniform, reflecting pride, identity, and the state’s police ethos, and is awarded only once to a force. First Recipient: The Uttar Pradesh(UP) Police was the first state police force to receive this honour in 1952. About Uttarakhand: Chief Minister (CM)– Pushkar Singh Dhami Governor– General (Retired) Gurmit Singh Capital- Dehradun Wildlife Sanctuary (WLS) – Govind WLS, Nandhaur WLS

# Page 28^page=28
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 28 Daily Content PDF APPOINTMENTS & RESIGNATIONS Myanmar Parliament Elects Min Aung Hlaing as President In April 2026, Min Aung Hlaing, Senior General and former Commander-in-Chief of the Tatmadaw (Armed Forces of Myanmar), was elected as the 11th President of Myanmar by the Pyidaungsu Hluttaw (Assembly of the Union), the legislature of Myanmar. • He succeeded U Myint Swe, the acting President, who passed away in October 2025. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Appointment of 11th President of Myanmar ✓ Who? Min Aung Hlaing ✓ Where? Naypyidaw, Myanmar ✓ Predecessor: U Myint Swe (acting President) ✓ Votes / Data: 429/584 votes; parliament dominated by USDP ✓ Vice-Presidents: Nan Ni Ni Aye (Karen State), U Nyo Saw. Background: Election: The election took place in a parliament dominated by the military-backed Union Solidarity and Development Party (USDP) and appointed armed forces representatives. Outcome: Min Aung Hlaing won 429 of 584 votes, while Nan Ni Ni Aye, regional Member of Parliament (MP) from Karen State, and U Nyo Saw were elected as Vice-Presidents of Myanmar. About Min Aung Hlaing: Military Career: He joined the Tatmadaw (Myanmar Armed Forces) and steadily rose through the ranks, becoming Commander-in-Chief in 2011and served as a Senior General until March 2026, playing a key role in military operations and national security strategy. Coup: Effectively ruled Myanmar after leading the 2021 military coup that ousted the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi and dissolved the National League for Democracy (NLD). Presidency: Relinquished his military post to comply with the constitution, which prohibits the President from simultaneously holding the top military position, before assuming the office of President. About Myanmar: Capital – Naypyidaw Currency – Myanmar Kyat (MMK) Krishna Kumar Singh Takes Additional Charge as SAIL CMD Following Amarendu Prakash’s Resignation In April 2026, Krishna Kumar Singh, Director (Personnel) at Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL), took additional charge as Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) for a three-month interim period (2 April to 1 July 2026). • This followed the resignation of Amarendu Prakash, effective 1 April 2026, which was approved by the Ministry of Steel (MoS). Exam Hints: ✓ What? Appointment of interim CMD of SAIL & CMD of POWERGRID ✓ CMD of SAIL: Krishna Kumar Singh ✓ Predecessor: Amarendu Prakash (Resigned on 1 April 2026) ✓ Tenure: For 3 months (2 April to 1 July 2026) ✓ CMD of POWERGRID: Burra Vamsi Rama Mohan ✓ Predecessor: Dr. Ravindra Kumar Tyagi ✓ Tenure: Till 31 July 2030

# Page 29^page=29
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 29 Daily Content PDF About Krishna Kumar Singh: Career: Nearly 40 years at SAIL, starting in 1987 as a Management Trainee at Bhilai Steel Plant, with early experience in the Blooming & Billet Mill before moving to Human Resource Development (HRD). Expertise: Made significant contributions across Operations, Human Resource Development (HRD), Vigilance, and Personnel & Administration (P&A). Leadership: Rose through key positions including Executive Director (ED) (In-Charge) Personnel & Administration (P&A), and was appointed Director (Personnel) in 2022. POWERGRID Appoints Burra Vamsi Rama Mohan as its CMD In April 2026, the board of Power Grid Corporation of India Limited (POWERGRID) approved the appointment of Burra Vamsi Rama Mohan as its Chairman and Managing Director (CMD), with his tenure effective from April 1, 2026, until his superannuation on July 31, 2030, or until further orders, as per the Ministry of Power (MoP). • He succeeds Dr. Ravindra Kumar Tyagi, who demitted office on March 31, 2026, upon attaining the mandatory age of superannuation. About Burra Vamsi Rama Mohan: Experience: Over 30 years of experience in power transmission and telecom sectors, handling projects, procurement, regulatory affairs, and asset management. Leadership: Served as Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of POWERGRID Teleservices Limited, driving telecom expansion and initiating the first data centre, and also held the role of Director (Projects) at POWERGRID until July 31, 2030, or until further orders. Regulatory: Founding member of POWERGRID’s Regulatory Cell, playing a crucial role in shaping the organisation’s regulatory strategy. About Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL): It was established on January 24, 1973 replacing the erstwhile Hindustan Steel Limited (HSL) which was established in 1954 and is classified as a ‘Maharatna’ Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE). Headquarters- New Delhi, Delhi SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY Union Minister Rajnath Singh Commissioned Advanced Stealth Frigate ‘INS Taragiri’ in Visakhapatnam, AP In April 2026, Union Minister Rajnath Singh, Ministry of Defence (MoD) formally commissioned the advanced stealth frigate Indian Naval Ship (INS) Taragiri (F41) into the Indian Navy (IN) at Naval Dockyard in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh (AP). • Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) Anil Chauhan; Admiral Dinesh Kumar (DK) Tripathi, Chief of Naval Staff (CNS), IN; Captain Jagmohan (Retd.), Chairman and Managing Director (CMD) of Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL), were among those present during the commissioning. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Commissioning of Advanced Stealth Frigate into IN ✓ Frigate Name: INS Taragiri (F41) ✓ Commissioned by: Union Minister Rajnath Singh, MoD ✓ Where? Naval Dockyard (Visakhapatnam, AP) ✓ Built by: Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited ✓ Designed by: Warship Design Bureau ✓ Preceded by: INS Nilgiri, INS Udaygiri, INS Himgiri ✓ Replaces: Leander-class INS Taragiri (1980–2013)

# Page 30^page=30
Report Errors in the PDF - support@affairscloud.com Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 30 Daily Content PDF ✓ Developed under: Project 17A About INS Taragiri: Design & Lineage: INS Taragiri, the fourth stealth frigate under Project 17A, has been designed by the Warship Design Bureau (WDB) and built by Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL). • It follows the earlier vessels: INS Nilgiri, INS Udaygiri, and INS Himgiri. Predecessor: This newly commissioned stealth frigate joins the Eastern Fleet on the eastern seaboard, replacing the Leander-class frigate of the same name that served in the Indian Navy from 1980 to 2013. Arms and Ammunition: The vessel features a vast range of weapons including Supersonic Surface-to- Surface missiles; Medium-range Surface-to-Air Missiles (MRSAM); advanced anti-submarine warfare system; and advanced indigenous Sound Navigation and Ranging (SONAR) systems, among others.
